clue.text: Lack of sincerity in tournament directors, nothing more

indicators.note: more here means 'plus', adding the last piece on

parts.note: a cup is a knockout competition, such as the FA Cup
a company's directors sit on its board
love is zero in tennis scoring

explanation.surface: A complaint that the people running a competition are insincere and offer nothing extra.
explanation.walkthrough: In the cricket-free British sense, love is the tennis word for a zero score.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes affection shown only for what one can get, as a pet fawns on whoever opens the food store; hence insincerity.

clue.text: Just like a superhero to secure company in part of Massachusetts

indicators.note: to secure is to hold something fast within, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: superheroes such as Superman wear capes, so are caped

explanation.surface: A comic-book hero is pictured protecting a firm somewhere in New England.
explanation.definitionFit: The hooked peninsula and its towns form a well-known region of the US state, a summer holiday area.

clue.text: Concert getting zero advertising material

parts.note: a prom is a promenade concert, as at the BBC Proms in London
the figure 0 looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: A concert that draws no publicity at all.
explanation.definitionFit: A promo is short for a promotion: a trailer, video or leaflet used to publicise something.

clue.text: Ring flat cancelling time for free access

parts.note: a ring is round, like the letter O

indicators.note: cancelling something removes it, so a letter is struck out of the flat

parts.note: a penthouse is a top-floor flat

explanation.surface: Someone telephones about a flat, calling off an appointment, to secure free entry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring' tempts as 'phone', but here it stands for the round letter; the flat in question is a top-floor one.
explanation.definitionFit: An event where a home or institution welcomes all visitors without invitation is an unrestricted, free-entry occasion.

clue.text: The way staff will cluster round one

indicators.note: to cluster round something is to surround it, so the staff encloses the other piece

parts.note: a rod is a staff or stick
A means one, as in 'a pound'

explanation.surface: Staff members gathering round a colleague, perhaps pointing the way.
explanation.definitionFit: A road is a route or path, a way from one place to another.

clue.text: What busy vacations seem to do, unfortunately

definitions.text: What busy vacations seem to do
definitions.meaning: a crowded holiday flies by and seems to be one day short, read as a phrase of three words
an old exclamation of regret, meaning alas

explanation.surface: A wry lament that hectic holidays always feel cut short.
explanation.walkthrough: Split into three words, the answer says what packed holidays appear to do; as one word it is an archaic cry of sorrow.
explanation.definitionFit: The archaic interjection expresses regret, so it can stand for a sigh of 'sadly, alas'.

clue.text: Permission to travel to take in the Northern view

indicators.note: taking in means enclosing, so the visa holds the other letter

parts.note: a visa is the stamp allowing entry to a country
in northern English dialect 'the' is shortened to t', so the northern 'the' is T

explanation.surface: Getting a visa to go north and enjoy the scenery.
explanation.walkthrough: Yorkshire and other northern English speech clips 'the' to t', as in 'down t' pit'.
explanation.definitionFit: A vista is a long, pleasing prospect or panorama, a synonym of view.

clue.text: Attractive meadows — long to go round them?

indicators.note: going round means surrounding, so the longing word wraps the meadows

parts.note: to long for something is to pant for it
a lea is a poetic word for a meadow

explanation.surface: Charming fields that make you want to stroll around them.
explanation.definitionFit: Pleasant means agreeable or appealing, which matches the sense of attractive.

clue.text: Lunar rocks filled with energy? Incredible

indicators.note: filled with means one piece has another put inside it
rocks as a verb means shakes, so the word Lunar is shaken into a new order

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Moon rocks charged with energy would be amazing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rocks' is the anagram signal, not moon samples: LUNAR becomes UNRAL, and 'filled with' puts E inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unreal seems too strange to be true, which is what incredible means.

clue.text: Prince, one in legendary castle, recalled description of solar system

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the castle with its insert is read backwards
in places the numeral inside the castle's name

parts.note: Camelot was King Arthur's castle in legend
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A prince in Arthur's castle remembers an account of the planets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts I into CAMELOT to give CIAMELOT; 'recalled' turns that round to TOLEMAIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Ptolemy's ancient model put the Earth at the centre with the Sun and planets circling it, an account of the heavens.

clue.text: Boy penning a line for literary gathering

indicators.note: penning means shutting in, as sheep in a pen, so the boy encloses the rest

parts.note: a son is a boy

explanation.surface: A lad writing a line of verse for a meeting of writers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penning' looks like writing, but here it means enclosing.
explanation.definitionFit: A salon is a regular meeting of writers and thinkers at a host's home, as in eighteenth-century Paris.

clue.text: Area of water included in church's garden feature

indicators.note: included in means put inside, so the water goes within the church letters

parts.note: CE stands for the Church of England
a loch is a Scottish lake

explanation.surface: A lake on church land counted as part of its grounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A cloche is a bell-shaped glass or plastic cover put over young plants in a garden.

clue.text: Reduced time with lower quantity of information

indicators.note: reduced means cut down, so the time word loses its final letter

parts.note: a date is a point in time
to abase is to lower or humble

explanation.surface: Cutting the time spent means receiving less information.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lower' looks like an adjective with 'quantity', but it is the verb ABASE.
explanation.definitionFit: A database is an organised store of facts and records, a body of information.

clue.text: Aggressive behaviour remains high?

parts.note: dust is what remains, as in 'ashes to ashes, dust to dust'
up means high, raised

explanation.surface: Wondering whether leftovers should be stored on a top shelf.
explanation.definitionFit: A dust-up is British slang for a brawl or quarrel, a bout of fighting.

clue.text: Elevated words, certainly, about bird life initially

indicators.note: about means around, so the certain word goes round the bird and the letter

parts.note: sure is used to mean certainly
a tit is a small songbird

indicators.note: initially means taking only the first letter of the word life

explanation.surface: Lofty language about the start of a bird's existence.
explanation.definitionFit: Surtitles are translated words projected above the stage during an opera, so they are text placed up high.

clue.text: Standard trouble about a second watersport item

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the standard and trouble words go round the other pieces

parts.note: par is the standard or norm, as in golf
to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: Ordinary difficulty concerning a second piece of beach kit.
explanation.definitionFit: A parasail is a parachute-like canopy that lifts a rider while towed by a boat.

clue.text: Rock group excited the Maoris

indicators.note: excited means stirred up, so the letters of the words the Maoris are agitated into a new order

explanation.surface: New Zealand's Maori people thrilled by a rock band.
explanation.definitionFit: Aerosmith is the American hard rock band behind 'Dream On' and 'Walk This Way'.

clue.text: French composer getting the story right

parts.note: the message is the gist, the story being told

explanation.surface: A French musician understanding the narrative correctly.
explanation.definitionFit: André Messager was a French composer and conductor of operettas such as 'Véronique'.

clue.text: This writer gives way after first appearance of racing car

indicators.note: after puts the yielding word behind the letter from racing

parts.note: a setter calls themself 'this writer', giving ME

indicators.note: the first appearance of a word is its opening letter, here from racing

parts.note: to cede is to give way or yield

explanation.surface: A writer yields to a racing car that has just appeared.
explanation.definitionFit: Mercedes-Benz is the German maker of luxury cars and Formula One racers.

clue.text: Start to mark cryptic clue's strength

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, here from mark
cryptic means puzzling or obscure, so the letters of the clue's word are jumbled

parts.note: the word clue's gives the five letters of clues for shuffling

explanation.surface: Instructions to begin scoring the power of a puzzle clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Muscle means power or force, as in 'financial muscle'.

clue.text: Leader of government suppressing memory for now

indicators.note: suppressing means holding something down within, so the leader encloses the memory

parts.note: PM is the prime minister, who leads a British government
rote is learning by memory

explanation.surface: A prime minister keeping recollections quiet for the time being.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leader of government' looks like a first-letter instruction but is PM.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase is short for pro tempore, meaning temporarily, for the time being.

clue.text: Created one recipe, getting a type of cake

parts.note: made means created
I is the Roman numeral for one
R is the abbreviation for recipe, from Latin recipe, take

explanation.surface: Following one recipe to bake a particular cake.
explanation.definitionFit: A Madeira cake is a plain, firm British sponge, traditionally eaten with Madeira wine.

clue.text: Scientist's first equipment shattered this, being unsteady

indicators.note: first takes only the opening letter of the word Scientist's

parts.note: kit is equipment

indicators.note: shattered means broken in pieces, so the word this is rearranged

explanation.surface: A scientist's apparatus breaks, leaving the lab in a wobbly state.
explanation.definitionFit: Skittish means nervous, jumpy and unpredictable, which matches being unsteady.

clue.text: Name of herb occurring in sentence on the radio

indicators.note: on the radio means heard, not seen, so the word is judged by how it is said

parts.note: time is a prison sentence, as in 'doing time'

explanation.surface: A herb's name mentioned in a broadcast sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: Thyme is a fragrant culinary herb of the mint family.

clue.text: Ski resort gets emptied a bit — avalanche's heading in

indicators.note: emptied means the inside letters are removed, keeping only the outside ones of gets
in puts the avalanche's letter inside the little bit

parts.note: a tad is a small amount, a bit

indicators.note: heading means the first letter of avalanche's

explanation.surface: A ski resort is slightly cleared out as an avalanche heads its way.
explanation.definitionFit: Gstaad is a fashionable Alpine resort in the Bernese Oberland, Switzerland.

clue.text: A lot of hackneyed stuff in housing classification

parts.note: corn is trite, sentimental material, a load of it being hackneyed

explanation.surface: Plenty of tired clichés found in a scheme for grading homes.
explanation.definitionFit: ACORN, A Classification Of Residential Neighbourhoods, is a British system sorting areas by housing and residents for marketing.

clue.text: A woman saying farewell to son sadly

indicators.note: saying farewell means letting go, so the abbreviation is removed from the woman

parts.note: a lass is a young woman

explanation.surface: A mother bidding her boy goodbye with sorrow.
explanation.definitionFit: Alas is an interjection of grief or regret, used like 'unfortunately' or 'sadly'.

clue.text: Ready to relax by end of day

parts.note: to loll is to lounge or relax

indicators.note: end of takes only the final letter of the word day

explanation.surface: Prepared to unwind by the close of the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ready' is not 'prepared' but a noun: British slang 'the ready' is cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are British slang for money, so cash in hand can be called either.

clue.text: I behold endless devastation back in war zone

indicators.note: back means the joined pieces are read in reverse order

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning behold, look

indicators.note: endless means losing the final letter of the devastation word

parts.note: pillage is plunder and devastation

explanation.surface: Someone surveys endless destruction in a battle zone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts PILLAGE to PILLAG; 'back' turns ILOPILLAG round.
explanation.definitionFit: Gallipoli, in Turkey, was the site of the bloody 1915–16 Allied campaign of the First World War.

clue.text: What could make you uneasier than debilitation?

indicators.note: the phrase says these letters could be made into the answer by rearrangement, so the words uneasier than are shuffled

explanation.surface: Asking what could leave you more anxious than feeling weak.
explanation.definitionFit: Neurasthenia is an old medical term for nervous exhaustion and lassitude, a state of weakness.
